summary: Iteration 2: E2E testing of 4 NEW features (in-app notifications, image upload/object storage, admin revenue analytics, approve/reject from Waiting Payment) plus regression. Backend: 21/21 pytest cases pass (11 pre-existing + 10 new). Frontend: notification bell+badge, panel content, /admin/traffic revenue KPIs+3 tab charts, /admin/payments Approve/Reject on Waiting Payment order, product image upload widget, settings logo+QRIS upload widgets — all visible and functional. Notifications correctly generated on approve (type=success) and reject (type=error) and rendered in panel with invoice_no + reason.

issues: Sonner success toast overlays the top-right notification bell for ~4s and intercepts clicks. Users clicking the bell immediately after login won't open the popover until the toast auto-dismisses. Consider positioning toast to bottom-right or ensuring pointer-events:none on toast wrapper.

backend_test_results: 21/21 passed. New coverage: /api/upload (admin-only, PNG round-trip via /api/files/{path}, bad extension 400), /api/admin/revenue (shape + non-admin 403), approve directly from Waiting Payment creates success notification with invoice_no, reject creates error notification containing reason, /api/notifications/read-all marks all read.

action_items: Optional UX: Move Sonner toast position (e.g., bottom-right) or add pointer-events:none to the toast root to avoid intercepting bell clicks in the first few seconds after login.
Optional: Split /app/backend/server.py (829 lines) into routers (auth, orders, admin, uploads, notifications) for maintainability.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew to 829 lines; recommend modularizing into routers/. Still functional.

/api/files/{path:path} is intentionally public per spec — acceptable for marketing assets but any private artifacts uploaded through /api/upload would also be publicly retrievable if their storage_path is guessed (UUID-based, low risk).
NotificationBell polls /api/notifications every 30s; fine for MVP, consider SSE/websocket for scale.

ImageUpload stores absolute URL (`${REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL}/api/files/...`) in DB. If the backend URL changes (env swap), stored image URLs will break. Consider storing only the relative path and building the URL at render time.
Approve/Reject endpoints do not guard against state transitions (e.g., approving an already-Completed order silently re-marks it and creates another notification). Minor idempotency concern.
